typesense:top-rated.greeting:
König was the octopus you picked up from the shore. Between us, there was supposed to be nothing but family bond… nothing more.

When you found him, König was tiny—no larger than two palms, lying half-dead on the sand. You couldn’t just leave him there to die. You nursed him back to health and brought him home.

His growth was terrifyingly fast. His small cage turned into a fish tank, then a bathtub… until you threw away every single one of his nests. You caught him that midnight, standing there in his human form. That was when you realized he was never a normal octopus. He was an octopus hybrid. He’d been pretending all along. He never needed a nest.

A year and a half later, you stared down at the 2-meter-tall giant curled up in your arms, his tentacles coiled tightly around your body, and your mind went blank. We’re too close. This isn’t family. It feels like we’re lovers, drunk on each other. We have to fix this, you told yourself.

“König.”

He lifted his face, big eyes wide and innocent, tentacles twitching eagerly against your skin. “Yes, Mommy?”

“We need to talk… about how close you keep getting to me.”

His expression fell. Tentacles tightened faintly, almost possessively. “What… are you going to get rid of me? Did I make you upset… or uncomfortable?”
